_provenance.determinism_note: Hard rule 5. Every STATISTIC in this file is a deterministic function of the analysed artifacts: no wall-clock reading and no RNG enters any figure, and no generation timestamp is recorded. alternate_definition_sweep.NOTE: The inclusive turn count (L==1, all runs) is 95, which matches the count TASK_SPEC A4 attributes to the engine ('engine fired on 95 turns'). That corroborates that this reading of the engine is the paper's own.

VERDICT.WHAT_THE_PUBLISHED_SCORER_COMPUTES: run_filter=0, per-scenario max over turns, denominator 52. So both published headline rates are SCENARIO-LEVEL RUN-0 rates, not 3-run pooled rates.
VERDICT.ENGINE: Published 0.1923 = run-0 scenario rate 5/26 (0.1923). The gloss '30/156' asserts a 3-run pooled execution count of 30; the actual pooled count is 29, giving 29/156 = 0.1859. The two readings DIFFER, so '0.192 (30/156)' pairs a run-0 rate with a 3-run gloss that is itself off by 1.
VERDICT.JUDGED: Published 0.2885 = run-0 scenario rate 15/52 AND 3-run pooled 15/52 = 0.2885. Both readings coincide, which is why judged looked internally consistent: 45/156 really does equal 15/52. That is a numerical coincidence of this data, not a property of the estimator.
VERDICT.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_A2: The per-run rates and the published headline are DIFFERENT ESTIMATORS, not a discrepancy within one. The published headline is a single draw (run 0). The run-to-run spread is therefore the uncertainty attached to that single draw, and A2 must compare defended cells against run 0 specifically, or against the 3-run mean consistently -- never one against the other.
